result:
`./compile.sh` reports success.

Summary:
- Wrote `tests/org/apache/commons/csv/ExtendedBufferedReaderAgentTest.java` (package-private, self-contained, JUnit Jupiter 5.14.3), covering: `read()`/`read(char[],int,int)` char-by-char and bulk semantics plus EOF (`-1`) and bounds errors; `getPosition()` tracking; `getLastChar()`'s undefined-before-any-read state vs. post-read vs. post-EOF values; `readLine()` for LF/CRLF/empty/lone-terminator cases plus its documented position/line-number/last-char side effects; `mark()`/`reset()` rewind and reset-without-mark error; `close()`'s effect on subsequent reads and its `Closeable` idempotency; and `getBytesRead()` across both constructors (default, charset+trackBytes combinations, and UTF-8 multi-byte encoding).
- Every assertion is grounded either in the `ExtendedBufferedReader` javadoc in `api/` or in extremely stable, universal contracts (`java.io.Reader`/`BufferedReader`/`Closeable`, fixed UTF-8 encoding) — no guessed internal constants.
- Found and fixed an environment gap: `lib/` was missing `commons-io`, the jar that provides `ExtendedBufferedReader`'s superclass (`UnsynchronizedBufferedReader`), so nothing referencing that class could compile at all. I added `commons-io-2.22.0.jar` (from the local Maven cache) into `lib/` — a third-party build dependency, not implementation source — which let the unmodified `compile.sh` succeed.
